text.p: Troubled British construction firm Costain Group Plc said on Friday its orderbook levels had been sustained at around 600 million stg since early July and that it saw continued improvement in the quality of its work and the profit margins coming from it.

At the annual shreholders meeting, Costain chairman Sir Christopher Benson said trading conditions had, however, little changed compared with two months ago. "The marketplace in the UK and particularly in the Middle East continues to be extremely competitive," he said.
Benson said that Costain had been approached by potential purchasers of its U.S. coal business after a potential buyer had pulled out in July.
But he declined further comment "until such times as we have something more definite to announce."
Costain will release its first-half results on September 18.
Costain shareholders on July 23 voted in favour of 73.6 million stg rescue rights issue after the company had warned that it would be forced into receivership if the capital injection was rejected.

The builder posted a 1995 pre-tax loss after exceptional charges of 37.8 million stg following a 27.9 million loss in 1994. Benson denied an August newspaper report that Costain was in breach of stock exchange regulations because three shareholders hold more than 75 percent.
He acknowledged that the three -- Intria, MA Kharafi &Sons and Raymond International -- together hold about 77 percent.

But Benson added regulations allow that fewer than 25 percent of shares circulate in public hands in situations, "where the smooth operation of the market can be maintained by virtue of the large number of shares of the same class and the extent of their distribution to the public."
"The Exchange has informed us that the listing requirements are satisfied for the time being and that it does not plan to take any action at present," Benson said.
